decision.reason: Both candidates are Kailh Choc v1 low-profile switches that fit the slot, so either would work. The request does not specify a switch feel, and tactile Browns are the more common default for a general-purpose typing keyboard, so I picked C1

payload.message: 1 of 5 slots decided

decision.reason: The slot needs 61 keycaps for a Choc low-profile board. The standard 1u KLP Lame keycap is the base unit that makes up most of a 61-key layout, whereas the 1.5u, homing, and thumb variants are specialty pieces needed only in small numbers.

decision.reason: For a low-profile Choc keyboard, a small SMD switching diode is the standard choice for the key matrix. The 1N4148W in SOD-123 is the usual pick: it is easy to hand-solder and widely used in keyboard PCBs. The through-hole DO-35 (C1) is too
